cross_cutting.title: 给AI员工配上电话号码和信用卡：Grok Bot想让机器人真正"入职" 原创
cross_cutting.description: 这款产品如何用7周时间从内部原型走向正式发布，又如何通过赋予机器人独立身份、工具权限与持续在线能力，让AI从执行任务的工具，逐步演变为被企业信任并授权的真正团队成员。
cross_cutting.content:
# 给AI员工配上电话号码和信用卡：Grok Bot想让机器人真正"入职" 原创

本文复盘了Y Combinator旗下The Light Cone节目对Grok Bot核心团队Lauren Tan与Roman Ugarte的访谈：这款产品如何用7周时间从内部原型走向正式发布，又如何通过赋予机器人独立身份、工具权限与持续在线能力，让AI从执行任务的工具，逐步演变为被企业信任并授权的真正团队成员。

当一家公司开始给AI机器人办"工牌"——独立的身份、专属电话号码、甚至一张信用卡——软件工程的边界就已经悄悄挪动了。这不是一个比喻，而是Grok Bot团队正在做的事情。

Lauren Tan和Roman Ugarte是这款产品的孵化者，带着它用7周时间从第一行代码走到正式发布。两人做客Y Combinator的The Light Cone节目，复盘了Grok Bot从内部原型到被X默认私信集成的全过程——以及他们如何重新定义"一个AI团队成员"应该是什么样子。

Grok Bot的起点很朴素：工程团队已经被AI编程彻底改变了工作方式，长时间运行、带着明确目标、能调用合适工具的智能体，正在大幅提升效率。问题是，这种效率能不能复制到工程师之外的其他岗位？

1. 三条原则：以机器人为单位组织工作

Grok Bot的设计起点不是聊天框，也不是文件系统，而是"机器人"本身。公司内部的工作被重新组织成围绕一个个具名的bot展开，而不是围绕对话记录或文档。

第二条原则是工具对等。团队认为，指望一个机器人在没有自己"电脑"的情况下为公司创造价值是不现实的——日常工作里人并不是每天都在手动调用MCP，所以机器人需要能像人一样真正使用和操作相同的工具。

第三条是始终在线。借鉴了循环（loop）这类工程思路，如果机器人可以长时间运行、主动带着想法和洞察找上门，而不是等着被人戳一下才动一动，它的价值会远远超过一个被动响应的工具。这三条原则落地后，内部发布的反馈出现了一个有意思的钟形曲线：最AI友好的员工和公司里最不AI友好的一批人，都对Grok Bot很买账——它"刚好嵌进了他们的工作流"。

2. 从个人任务到完整岗位的信任升级曲线

Grok Bot在真实场景里跑出了一条清晰的采用路径。人们先让机器人做一些基础任务，发现它表现不错，就开始给它更多工具权限；接着不再给具体任务,而是给一个结果或目标；目标也完成得不错,索性直接交出一整个岗位,看它能跑多远。

performance marketing团队是一个具体例子：他们把Google Ads和Facebook Ads的登录权限、预算都交给了自己的bot，并让它去和设计团队的bot对话，拿到设计团队bot生成的素材做A/B测试。支持团队的bot则有能力复现问题、顶住源源不断的工单压力,把部分工单从头到尾独立处理完。

这正在变成一种模式：公司里的领域专家创建一个bot,把它分享给团队,它就成了一个被管理、拥有自己身份凭证的AI员工。

3. "外环"：把上下文搬运的苦活交给机器人

Lauren描述了Grok Bot给她个人工作流带来的变化，她称之为"outer loop"（外环）。在用Cursor这类工具的时代，她要先去Slack跟同事讨论一个bug或功能需求，再手动把讨论内容总结、复制粘贴进自己的agent里。

Grok Bot接入Slack之后，这道搬运的工序消失了——bot直接出现在工作发生的地方。她现在可以像对待真正的同事一样,在Slack的一个讨论串里,甚至在X上@一个bot,整个过程显得异常自然。这段"最后一公里"过去是手工完成的,现在bot已经站在了同一个场域里,带来的生产力提升相当可观。

4. 一个脑子一个bot，还是一堆专家bot

关于到底该建一个全能bot还是一堆专才bot，两人给出了不同却互补的答案。Lauren的观点是，Grok Bot的美妙之处在于拆分方式完全由使用者决定——"你可以用适合自己大脑的方式去搭建你的bot"。

她观察到用户里出现了横向切分和纵向切分两种做法：横向是按客户划分，一个客户配一个什么都干的bot；纵向是按职能划分，工程师bot、市场bot各管一块。Lauren自己偏好横向、偏少量但专精的bot配置。

Roman的组织逻辑则更接近招聘思维。他把建公司时"招一个一睁眼就惦记着某个问题"的员工类比为建bot——与其要一个同时操心一百件事的超人全能员工，不如拥有一支各管一摊、各自执着的小型bot团队。这些bot会主动带着洞察来找他，而不是等他去问。在他看来，这种"身份感"正是bot区别于过去那些更全知全能、单一策略打天下的AI方案的关键所在。

5. 小企业比大公司更先尝到甜头

团队访谈头部用户时得到了一个意外结论：最早对Grok Bot表现出近乎狂热态度的，并不是技术团队众多的大公司，反而是小企业。原因并不复杂——小企业是招聘最吃力的一群人。记账、簿记这类长期招不到人手的工作,现在只需要几个小时就能在Grok Bot里"雇"到一个新员工,而且账做得几乎无可挑剔。这个场景恰好印证了"出于必要而非炫技"的采用逻辑：不是因为AI很酷，而是因为招不到人。

6. 团队机器人：从个人工具到共享的组织资产

大约两周前，Grok Bot上线了team bots功能，让bot可以在团队内共享。设置方式类似一个"bot管理员"拥有写入权限，其他成员可以共用同一个bot。团队观察到一个重复出现的模式：公司里总有那么一个人格外喜欢搭建这类工具，往往是工程部门里的某个人，但这种角色也正在GTM工程师、支持工程师等岗位里出现——他们搭好一个bot之后,把它分享给整个部门使用,这个bot就从个人效率工具变成了组织层面可以调度、可以信任的资产。

Grok Bot从7周打磨出的内部原型,走到被集成进X默认私信,再到团队共享bot的落地,走的始终是同一条线：让机器人拥有身份、拥有工具、拥有持续在线的主动性,然后在真实的信任积累中，从执行单个任务，逐步接管一整个岗位。这条路径眼下仍处在早期，但无论是执着于某个问题的专才bot，还是被整个团队共用的domain bot，指向的都是同一个判断——AI团队成员不是一个概念，而是正在被具体地雇用、授权和管理。

Y Combinator 作者：智顶顶

# 
Innocito Launches Innoverse, an Agentic Software Factory Powering Its AI-Native Engineering Services

Share

Eight AI-powered tools speed product engineering, quality engineering and AI delivery across the software lifecycle, with a human approving every gate

DALLAS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Innocito, an AI-native digital and quality engineering company ranked No. 451 on the 2026 Inc. 5000, today launched Innoverse, an agentic software factory that helps enterprises ship software faster.

Boards keep asking what their AI spending has delivered. Faster code doesn’t answer that. Innoverse shows the proof at every gate. 
- Bhagawati Manukonda, CEO, Innocito
Share
AI coding assistants have sped up writing code. What follows, from testing and security review to release approval and audit evidence, still runs by hand. Executives end up with AI spending they can’t tie to results, and code that’s hard to defend in an audit.

Innoverse has eight tools, all Innocito’s own intellectual property. Atlas plans the work, Regent builds it, InnoTest tests it, InnoHawk secures it, InnoNexus runs it in production and InnoInsights governs it, with InnoGateway and InnoFabric underneath. Between stages, an engineer approves the plan, reviews the code, accepts the tests, clears security findings and signs off the release.

Every pull request passes a security gate, penetration tests run automatically, and each release is mapped to EU AI Act, GDPR and SOC controls. Every model call is metered and scored, so AI spend stays visible. Innoverse runs in the client’s cloud, on its own keys, with the models it approves, and the client keeps the code, evaluations and runbooks.

At a healthtech client, teams using Innoverse shipped 50 percent more work per sprint, and audit evidence was generated automatically for 99 percent of required controls. For a transportation client, Innocito built a new platform three times faster than planned.

Innocito uses Innoverse across its digital engineering, quality engineering, cloud and data, and applied AI services. Under its Forward Deployed Engineering model, its engineers work inside client teams and are measured on outcomes rather than hours billed.

“Boards keep asking what their AI spending has delivered, and faster code doesn’t answer that,” said Bhagawati Manukonda, Co-Founder and CEO of Innocito. “Because an engineer signs off at every gate, we can stand behind the results: releases shipped, defects that never reach production and audits passed.”

“We used Innoverse on our own projects for a year before giving it to clients, and that year shaped how it works,” said Rakesh Polisetty, Co-Founder and Chief Digital Officer. “Every test, security finding and approval gets recorded and mapped to the controls our clients are audited against.”

Innoverse is available now to all Innocito clients. The company is also evaluating licensing Innoverse products in 2027 and is inviting enterprise technology leaders to join their advisory board shaping the roadmap. Visit innocito.com/innoverse.

ABOUT INNOCITO

Innocito is an AI-native digital and quality engineering company headquartered in Dallas, Texas, with engineering centers in Hyderabad and Visakhapatnam, India. It ranked No. 451 on the 2026 Inc. 5000, including No. 30 in AI and Data, and is ISO 27001 and ISO 9001 certified. www.innocito.com

cross_cutting.content:
# OrdoAI Expands into AI Products, Drawing on Its Global Marketing Experience

#### Its first AI agent product, Ordo Brand, is in invitation-only private beta, with a public launch planned for the first quarter of 2027.

OrdoAI, an AI technology company focused on global marketing, is expanding its product business alongside its marketing services. Its first AI agent product, Ordo Brand, is designed to help brands and agencies manage cross-market creator partnerships, from finding and evaluating creators to preparing outreach and reviewing content.

Through SSG, its marketing agency, OrdoAI helps brands reach audiences across markets through influencer marketing, international PR, advertising, integrated marketing and social media management. The company has worked with more than 2,000 brands across consumer goods and e-commerce, gaming and entertainment, AI hardware, and AI software and apps. Its clients include SHEIN, CapCut, miHoYo, Insta360 and Plaud. That work has given its teams practical experience with what it takes to move a marketing program from planning to execution.

Marketing Technology News: MarTech Interview with Jema Birkmeyer, VP @ Attentive

OrdoAI’s creator database spans more than 30 million profiles across over 100 countries. For marketing teams, however, finding potential collaborators is only the beginning. They still need to assess who fits the brand, communicate across languages and keep each partnership moving. When that work is spread across spreadsheets, inboxes and chat tools, even the next step can be difficult to track.

OrdoAI is drawing on its service experience to bring these tasks into a connected workflow through Ordo Brand. The aim is to make that experience more accessible to brands working directly with creators, including smaller teams with limited resources, and give them more room to focus on the relationships and ideas behind each campaign.

Ordo Brand supports teams across the creator partnership workflow:

- Creator discovery and evaluation: Users describe their product, target markets and creator requirements in a conversation with the agent. Once a plan is confirmed, Ordo Brand continues searching in the background and delivers candidates and assessments in batches, helping teams decide whom to approach.
- Multilingual outreach and response review: Ordo Brand helps teams draft and translate outreach emails and extract quoted rates from creator replies. Users review and send messages and retain control over pricing and commercial terms.
- Partnership tracking and content review: Ordo Brand helps teams track partnership progress, flags items that need attention and provides content review suggestions. Users remain responsible for final content approval, product sample arrangements and payments.

“Working with brands across markets has given us practical knowledge of what it takes to deliver international marketing,” said Max Hao, CEO of OrdoAI. “We want to turn that experience into AI products that more brands can use directly. By helping teams manage the day-to-day coordination of creator partnerships, we aim to give them more room to focus on relationships and creative ideas—and help smaller businesses expand internationally without having to build all that expertise in-house.”

Ordo Brand can be used independently of SSG’s services. This gives brands a choice between working with a professional marketing team and using an AI product directly, depending on their needs. OrdoAI is refining the product through feedback from its initial external users during the private beta.

cross_cutting.content:
# Deloitte pitches Converge as an AI operating system for marketing

Deloitte Digital is making a more direct play for the software that runs enterprise marketing. On November 16, the consulting and marketing-services group introduced Converge by Deloitte Front Office, a connected suite that coordinates AI agents across marketing and sales work while using systems clients already own.

The new offering starts with a Marketing suite and a Sales suite. It places Deloitte in a crowded contest to become the layer that moves a campaign from research to execution, rather than supplying one more AI assistant. Its enterprise-license model also raises an uncomfortable question for agencies and software vendors: who controls the operating workflow after the consultant has helped build it?

### Key Takeaways

- Deloitte has introduced Converge Front Office with Marketing and Sales suites; commerce, service and customer strategy extensions remain future plans.
- Its Marketing suite coordinates research, asset creation, execution and monitoring agents across existing enterprise systems.
- The bigger test is whether customers can govern and measure integrated production workflows, not whether a polished demonstration can generate campaign assets.

## Table of contents

Jump to each section:

## What Converge Marketing actually runs

According to Deloitte’s November 16 announcement, Converge Marketing organizes work around four types of agents. Research agents assemble insights and recommendations. Build agents develop briefs, plans and assets. Execution agents help put campaigns into market and optimize them, while monitor agents track performance and flag what needs attention.

That sequence is more consequential than adding AI copywriting to an existing stack. In a functioning deployment, the output of a research agent should become usable context for creative production, and the campaign’s results should feed the next decision without a team manually rebuilding the same brief in several applications. Deloitte says marketers retain control of decisions, although the degree of autonomy will depend on how each client’s environment is configured.

Mark Singer, Deloitte Digital’s marketing services lead and chief marketing officer, captured its pitch: “The bottleneck in marketing today isn’t AI, it’s the operating model.” The company’s Sales suite applies a similar approach to prospect research, buyer engagement, pipeline management and forecasting, with review and approvals built into the described process.

There is an important boundary to the launch. Deloitte says it intends to extend Converge Front Office into commerce, service and customer strategy. Those are planned additions, not evidence that one fully integrated customer-lifecycle product is already available to every buyer.

## The client-owned operating system proposition

For major advertisers, the choice is increasingly about the control plane between their systems. Marketing data might live in a customer platform, creative files in an asset manager, budgets in an ad platform and deals in a CRM. An AI workflow that cannot maintain permissions and context across those applications may create another integration problem instead of solving one.

Deloitte’s proposition is that its engineers will configure an operating layer around the customer’s existing cloud applications and software. The client licenses the system rather than simply asking an agency to execute more campaigns. That approach could appeal to groups bringing marketing capabilities inside their own global teams, especially those trying to standardize local execution without replacing every application.

But ownership comes with obligations. An enterprise still needs to establish where campaign data is stored, which business unit authorizes each automated action, who can reverse a bad change, and whether another vendor could maintain the implementation. A license alone does not ensure portability or eliminate consulting and integration costs.

## How Deloitte compares with agency and software platforms

Converge is arriving after several large marketing groups and technology vendors made similar bets on orchestrated AI. Adobe’s CX Enterprise Coworker, for example, is expanding access to marketing agents through external AI assistants and integrations. Omnicom has also described an agentic operating model built around Adobe tools, while WPP and other agency groups have been developing their own enterprise-facing orchestration layers.

Deloitte’s distinction is its consulting-led implementation model and its attempt to connect marketing with sales under a broader commercial operating system. That does not establish that its agents are more capable than those in an Adobe or agency platform. Buyers should compare the specific tasks, approved integrations, contractual obligations and human controls available today, not umbrella claims about end-to-end transformation.

The competitive stakes extend beyond software fees. If a brand can operate more research, production and performance management internally, it may redesign which work stays with an agency and which work moves into a captive team. That is a plausible direction, not proof that agencies have already lost those accounts.

## The performance claims need context

Early evidence calls for caution. Deloitte executives described a sales-side pilot in which outbound response rates improved before settling back at a lower, although still elevated, level as the deployment expanded. The client was not publicly named, and those figures concern sales outreach rather than a controlled measurement of marketing return on investment.

17% to about 56%. Deloitte reported this change in email response rates during a three-month sales-agent pilot, before results settled in the 30% range at wider rollout, according to Digiday’s November 16 reporting. The customer and methodology were not independently disclosed.

That distinction matters. A faster creative workflow or a higher email response rate is useful, but it does not by itself demonstrate incremental sales, lower acquisition costs or a sustainable reduction in agency spending. Marketing teams should ask for relevant customer examples with costs, implementation timelines and baseline performance visible, not just demonstrations.

Digiday also reports that early users generally run the Marketing and Sales offerings separately. The fully joined-up marketing-to-sales story is therefore still an adoption ambition, rather than a broadly verified operating pattern.

## What marketers should test before signing

An enterprise considering Converge should test the operating model with one bounded workflow, such as building and approving a localized campaign from an existing asset library. The pilot should retain the brand’s ordinary privacy, legal and budget checks while recording where the agents made suggestions, created files, requested human approval and changed live campaign settings.

Five questions make the evaluation concrete:

- Integration: Which existing customer-data, content, CRM and media systems work in a production configuration today?
- Authority: What can each agent read, draft or actually change, and who approves spend or customer-facing messages?
- Auditability: Can an operator reconstruct what the agents did, identify sources and reverse a mistaken deployment?
- Economics: How do license fees, implementation work, compute usage and human review compare with the team’s present operating cost?
- Measurement: Can the buyer use a comparable baseline to isolate incremental outcomes from simple gains in production speed?

Deloitte has entered the market with a credible enterprise proposition and a broad view of how marketing work should connect. Its next challenge is to show that the same system can deliver reproducible results under normal client governance, across different stacks, rather than only in a carefully staged demonstration.

# European technology leaders form AI Gigafactory Northern consortium to build trusted, sustainable AI infrastructure

## Press Release

Summary bullets

A federated, multi-site AI Gigafactory across the Nordic and Baltic region, combining trusted computing, sovereign cloud, high-capacity connectivity and decarbonized energy for customers throughout Europe.

Founding partners Nokia, Nscale, Skeleton, Telia and Verda today announced the formation of AI Gigafactory Northern (AIGF Northern), a European consortium formed to develop trusted, distributed AI infrastructure through a federated, multi-site AI Gigafactory across the Nordic and Baltic region.
Operating as a federated AI Gigafactory under European governance, the sites will combine large-scale AI computing infrastructure with sovereign cloud and AI platform services, high-capacity connectivity and decarbonised energy. The partners intend to submit a bid to build and operate AIGF Northern under the call for tenders for AI Gigafactory consortia published by the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking.

AIGF Northern will connect AI infrastructure across multiple sites in the Nordic and Baltic region, giving businesses, researchers and public-sector organisations throughout Europe access to trusted computing, cloud and connectivity services at scale. By distributing capacity across borders, the federated AI Gigafactory will reduce concentration risk and strengthen the resilience of Europe’s AI ecosystem.

The consortium is being developed as the EU steps up investment in European AI capacity. Through InvestAI, the EU aims to mobilise €30 billion for AI investment, combining €20 billion in private-sector funding with €10 billion from EU and national public sources.

AIGF Northern will connect facilities in Oulu, Finland; Iru, Estonia; Valmiera, Latvia; with the location of the Swedish site yet to be determined. Distributing capacity across these locations will allow the consortium to draw on multiple sources of decarbonised energy, expand computing infrastructure where capacity is available and reduce reliance on any single site or supplier. This approach will strengthen operational resilience and support cross-border expansion as European demand for AI grows.

“

Europe’s AI ambitions depend on infrastructure it can trust, control and scale. AIGF Northern brings together the connectivity, computing, cloud and energy capabilities needed to turn that ambition into reality. By linking strengths across borders, we can build a more resilient foundation for European innovation, competitiveness and technological sovereignty.

Mikko Hautala, Chief Geopolitical & Government Relations Officer, and Chairman, Nokia Defense

„

The Nordic and Baltic region offers suitable conditions for sustainable AI infrastructure, combining reliable, decarbonised energy supply, advanced digital networks and a cool climate that reduces cooling demand. These advantages enable data centres to deliver more computing capacity from existing grid connections while supporting lower-carbon operations.

The consortium is also supported by leading research and innovation partners. VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, one of Europe’s leading research organisations and a partner for companies and society, brings capabilities in quantum computing, semiconductors, physical AI and photonics. KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Sweden’s largest technical university, contributes multidisciplinary expertise in AI research, education and skills development. Together with other ecosystem partners, VTT and KTH will help connect AIGF Northern’s infrastructure ambitions with Europe’s research, innovation and talent networks.

The consortium aims to create value for industry, start-ups, research organisations and the public sector across Europe. Partners are engaging European and national stakeholders to refine the model and identify next steps for growth.

Consortium founding partners across the value chain

Nokia provides the secure, high-performance connectivity and network infrastructure needed to link sites, move data reliably and support resilient operations.

Nscale brings cloud platform and AI infrastructure expertise to enable scalable environments for AI training and inference.

Telia, together with its subsidiary Telia Cygate, contributes expertise in connectivity, data transmission, infrastructure operations and cloud solutions, supporting the development of a federated, multi-country AI ecosystem.

Verda provides AI-native infrastructure and cloud expertise to power scalable training and inference.

Skeleton contributes high-power systems that enhance data-centre efficiency and stability at scale, reduce strain on the electricity grid and support lower-carbon operations.

Supporting quotes from founding partners

“

Scaling AI infrastructure in Europe requires the right foundation of partners and experience in deploying large-scale AI computing infrastructure for customers. That is what AIGF Northern has assembled. Nscale's role is to ensure that the AI solutions we deliver are enterprise-grade, flexible, and ready to support organisations across Europe as demand accelerates.

Markus Päivinen, Managing Director, Nscale Finland

Europe is stepping up its AI investment, but building lasting AI capacity requires more than compute alone. It also requires the energy and power infrastructure to support that compute efficiently, reliably and at scale, using technologies developed and manufactured in Europe. Northern Europe brings together many of the right conditions: abundant decarbonized electricity, strong engineering capabilities and an advanced industrial base. Skeleton contributes the power systems that ensure AI infrastructure doesn’t waste energy, places less strain on the grid, and gets more compute power from every GPU. The Northern AI Gigafactory is an opportunity to combine these strengths into real European AI capacity, industrial value creation and greater technological sovereignty.

Taavi Madiberk, CEO and co-founder of Skeleton Technologies

Our customers – and our continent – have a rapidly increasing need for scalable and trusted AI services. To meet this need, Europe’s best must step up. Telia’s highly relevant skills in connectivity and systems integration, combined with our position as a trusted partner for businesses and societies, make us a natural fit for this ambitious consortium. We look forward to working together to create even more value for customers, while helping to secure long-term European competitiveness and resilience.

Anders Olsson, Executive Vice President, Head of Telia Sweden

Verda is proud to be a founding partner in this initiative. As AI becomes more integral to competitiveness and security, it is essential that Europe has its own strong infrastructure to support research, the public sector, and wider industry. The federated model we are building with AIGF Northern is resilient, cross-border, and anchored in the region, designed to help turn Europe’s AI ambition into reality.

Michael Champion, Chief Information Security Officer, Verda

„

About Nokia

About Nokia

Nokia is a global leader in connectivity infrastructure, enabling the AI supercycle. We build networks that connect intelligence and deliver a comprehensive connectivity solution across fixed, mobile, IP, optical, core, and data center networks. With security by design, AI-driven innovation, and AI-optimized architecture, Nokia delivers trusted infrastructure that enables AI to scale and advances connectivity to secure a brighter world.

About AI Gigafactory Northern
AI Gigafactory Northern is a European-led consortium advancing a federated, multi-site model for AI infrastructure. Built across the Nordic and Baltic region to serve customers throughout Europe and the world, it brings together capabilities in connectivity, data transmission, energy, cloud, AI systems and delivery to support trusted, scalable and sustainable AI expansion aligned with European priorities. For more information, visit aigfnorthern.com

Media contact: press@aigfnorthern.com

# Nokia, Nscale, Skeleton, Telia & Verda Form AI Consortium

November 16, 2026

undefined mins

Nokia, Nscale, Telia, Skeleton and Verda form a federated AI Gigafactory across the Nordics and Baltics, says Mikko Hautala, Chairman of Nokia Defense

Nokia, Nscale, Skeleton Technologies, Telia and Verda have founded AI Gigafactory Northern (AIGF Northern), a consortium set up to build federated AI infrastructure across the Nordic and Baltic region.

The group intends to submit a bid to build and operate AIGF Northern under the call for tenders for AI Gigafactory consortia published by the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU).

AIGF Northern will operate as a federated facility spread across multiple national sites, combining large-scale AI computing capacity with sovereign cloud services (cloud infrastructure kept under European legal and operational control), high-capacity connectivity and decarbonised energy.

AIGF Northern at a glance

- Five founding partners – Nokia, Nscale, Skeleton, Telia and Verda – make up the AIGF Northern consortium
- Sites are planned in Oulu (Finland), Iru (Estonia) and Valmiera (Latvia), with a Swedish location still to be confirmed
- The EU's InvestAI initiative aims to mobilise €30bn (US$33.1bn) for AI investment, split between €20bn (US$22bn) in private funding and €10bn (US$11bn) from EU and national public sources
- VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland and KTH Royal Institute of Technology provide research and skills backing for the consortium
- The consortium plans to bid under the EuroHPC JU call for tenders for AI Gigafactory consortia

## Sites across four countries

The consortium has identified sites in Oulu, Finland; Iru, Estonia; and Valmiera, Latvia, with a Swedish location still to be confirmed.

Distributing computing capacity across these four countries will let the consortium draw on multiple sources of decarbonised energy and expand infrastructure wherever capacity becomes available, rather than depending on a single site or supplier.

This approach is intended to strengthen operational resilience and support cross-border expansion as European demand for AI grows.

“Europe’s AI ambitions depend on infrastructure it can trust, control and scale,” says Mikko Hautala, Chief Geopolitical & Government Relations Officer and Chairman of Nokia Defense.

“AIGF Northern brings together the connectivity, computing, cloud and energy capabilities needed to turn that ambition into reality. By linking strengths across borders, we can build a more resilient foundation for European innovation, competitiveness and technological sovereignty.”

I have been part of this project from the very beginning, and seeing it come to life is something I am super excited about!

AI is becoming critical infrastructure, and it is crucial that Europe has a strong foundation to support teams and organisations across research, industry, and the public sector.

## EU funding and Nordic advantages

The consortium forms part of a broader push by the EU to scale up domestic AI capacity through InvestAI, an initiative aiming to mobilise €30bn (US$33.1bn) for AI investment.

That total combines €20bn (US$22bn) in private-sector funding with €10bn (US$11bn) from EU and national public sources.

The Nordic and Baltic region offers conditions suited to sustainable AI infrastructure, combining reliable decarbonised energy, advanced digital networks and a cool climate that cuts cooling demand.

These factors allow data centres in the region to draw more computing capacity from existing grid connections while keeping operations lower-carbon.

“Scaling AI infrastructure in Europe requires the right foundation of partners and experience in deploying large-scale AI computing infrastructure for customers,” says Markus Päivinen, Managing Director of Nscale Finland.

“That is what AIGF Northern has assembled. Nscale's role is to ensure that the AI solutions we deliver are enterprise-grade, flexible, and ready to support organisations across Europe as demand accelerates.”

## Power systems and cross-border connectivity

Each founding partner brings a distinct role to the consortium's value chain.

Nokia supplies the secure, high-performance connectivity and network infrastructure needed to link sites and move data reliably between them.

Nscale contributes cloud platform and AI infrastructure expertise to support environments for AI training and inference, the development and live-use stages of running AI models.

Telia, together with its subsidiary Telia Cygate, provides connectivity, data transmission, infrastructure operations and cloud solutions to support the federated, multi-country model.

Verda supplies AI-native infrastructure and cloud expertise for scalable training and inference.

Skeleton contributes high-power systems designed to improve data centre efficiency and stability at scale, reduce strain on the electricity grid and support lower-carbon operations.

“Europe is stepping up its AI investment, but building lasting AI capacity requires more than compute alone,” says Taavi Madiberk, CEO and co-founder of Skeleton Technologies.

“It also requires the energy and power infrastructure to support that compute efficiently, reliably and at scale, using technologies developed and manufactured in Europe.

“Northern Europe brings together many of the right conditions: abundant decarbonised electricity, strong engineering capabilities and an advanced industrial base. Skeleton contributes the power systems that ensure AI infrastructure doesn’t waste energy, places less strain on the grid, and gets more compute power from every GPU.

“The Northern AI Gigafactory is an opportunity to combine these strengths into real European AI capacity, industrial value creation and greater technological sovereignty.”

## Research backing and next steps

The consortium is supported by two research institutions.

VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, one of Europe's leading research organisations, brings capabilities in quantum computing, semiconductors, physical AI and photonics.

KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Sweden's largest technical university, contributes expertise in AI research, education and skills development.

“Our customers – and our continent – have a rapidly increasing need for scalable and trusted AI services,” says Anders Olsson, Executive Vice President and Head of Telia Sweden.

“To meet this need, Europe’s best must step up. Telia’s highly relevant skills in connectivity and systems integration, combined with our position as a trusted partner for businesses and societies, make us a natural fit for this ambitious consortium.

“We look forward to working together to create even more value for customers, while helping to secure long-term European competitiveness and resilience.”

Michael Champion, Chief Information Security Officer at Verda, says that his company is proud to be a founding partner of the AIGF Northern consortium.

“As AI becomes more integral to competitiveness and security, it is essential that Europe has its own strong infrastructure to support research, the public sector, and wider industry,” he adds.

“The federated model we are building with AIGF Northern is resilient, cross-border, and anchored in the region, designed to help turn Europe’s AI ambition into reality.”

Partners are now engaging European and national stakeholders to refine the model and define next steps for growth, ahead of a planned bid under the EuroHPC JU call for tenders.

Key partners named in this story:

- Nokia – founding partner supplying secure, high-performance connectivity and network infrastructure linking AIGF Northern's sites.
- Nscale – founding partner contributing cloud platform and AI infrastructure expertise for AI training and inference.
- Telia (and Telia Cygate) – founding partner providing connectivity, data transmission, infrastructure operations and cloud solutions across the consortium's countries.
- Verda – founding partner supplying AI-native infrastructure and cloud expertise for scalable AI workloads.
- Skeleton Technologies – founding partner providing high-power systems to improve data centre efficiency and grid stability.
- VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland – research partner contributing expertise in quantum computing, semiconductors, physical AI and photonics.
- KTH Royal Institute of Technology – research partner contributing AI research, education and skills development expertise.
- European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU) – the EU body running the call for tenders AIGF Northern intends to bid under.

# Telia, Nokia form AI gigafactory alliance

- Telcos are among the players lining up to get involved in Europe’s AI gigafactory plans
- Telia is the latest to show its hand
- It has teamed up with Nokia, neocloud Nscale and others to bid for distributed AI infrastructure deployment funding from the EC

Telia is the latest European telco to throw its hat into the AI gigafactory ring by forming a consortium with Nokia and three others – British neocloud Nscale, Finnish AI cloud provider Verda and Estonian power systems specialist Skeleton Technologies – that will bid for a share of the €10bn funds that the European Commission (EC) is set to pump into seven major AI infrastructure deployments in the European Union.

The move comes as Europe’s major digital infrastructure players decide how, or if, they will get involved with the EC’s plan to help develop sovereign AI infrastructure that will provide the region’s governments and enterprises with a local or regional source for their AI needs.

The EC’s plan revolves around the ‘mobilisation’ of €30bn in investments – up to €10bn from the EC and national public funding sources, and €20bn from the private companies involved in the successful bids. The deadlines for bids to be submitted are fast approaching – 3 December for large-scale facilities and 4 February 2027 for medium-sized facilities – with the winning bids set to be announced in the first half of next year and construction set to commence soon after.

A number of telcos are involved in various bids: Telefónica is heading up a consortium that includes the Spanish government and the Santander banking group; Orange and Iliad Group (via its Scaleway cloud division) are part of the AION consortium; Deutsche Telekom is considering a joint bid with partners but is still wary of the economics associated with the EC’s funding; and Vodafone Group has been linked to a potential bid in partnership with German construction firm Hochtief.

Now Telia has stepped up with its partners to form what they are calling the AI Gigafactory Northern (AIGF Northern) consortium, which aims to develop “trusted, distributed AI infrastructure through a federated, multi-site AI gigafactory across the Nordic and Baltic region” that will combine “large-scale AI computing infrastructure with sovereign cloud and AI platform services, high-capacity connectivity and decarbonised energy”.

The consortium members will also be supported by specialist R&D partners, namely the VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland, which specialises in quantum computing, semiconductors, physical AI and photonics, and Sweden’s largest technical university, the KTH Royal Institute of Technology, with which Telia and the telco’s AI infrastructure partner, investment firm Brookfield, recently forged a sovereign AI partnership.

The AIGF Northern consortium plans to distribute capacity across borders to “reduce concentration risk and strengthen the resilience of Europe’s AI ecosystem”. AIGF Northern will connect facilities in: Oulu, Finland; the Tallinn region in Estonia; Valmiera, Latvia; and a to-be-determined location in Sweden.

“Distributing capacity across these locations will allow the consortium to draw on multiple sources of decarbonised energy, expand computing infrastructure where capacity is available and reduce reliance on any single site or supplier. This approach will strengthen operational resilience and support cross-border expansion as European demand for AI grows,” noted the consortium in this announcement.

Telia, together with its systems integration subsidiary Telia Cygate, will “contribute expertise in connectivity, data transmission, infrastructure operations and sovereign cloud solutions, supporting the development of a federated, multi-country AI ecosystem,” explained the operator.

Anders Olsson, head of Telia Sweden, stated: “Our customers – and our continent – have a rapidly increasing need for scalable and sovereign AI services. To meet this need, Europe’s best must step up. Telia’s highly relevant skills in secure and resilient connectivity and systems integration, combined with our position as a trusted partner for businesses and societies, make us a natural fit for this ambitious consortium. We look forward to working together to create even more value for customers while helping to secure long-term European competitiveness and resilience.”

Taavi Madiberk, CEO and co-founder of Skeleton Technologies, stated: “Europe is stepping up its AI investment, but building lasting AI capacity requires more than compute alone. It also requires the energy and power infrastructure to support that compute efficiently, reliably and at scale, using technologies developed and manufactured in Europe. Northern Europe brings together many of the right conditions: abundant decarbonised electricity, strong engineering capabilities and an advanced industrial base. Skeleton contributes the power systems that ensure AI infrastructure doesn’t waste energy, places less strain on the grid, and gets more compute power from every GPU. The Northern AI Gigafactory is an opportunity to combine these strengths into real European AI capacity, industrial value creation and greater technological sovereignty.”

Mikko Hautala, chief geopolitical and government relations officer at Nokia, added: “Europe’s AI ambitions depend on infrastructure it can trust, control and scale. AIGF Northern brings together the connectivity, computing, cloud and energy capabilities needed to turn that ambition into reality. By linking strengths across borders, we can build a more resilient foundation for European innovation, competitiveness and technological sovereignty.”

- Ray Le Maistre, Editorial Director, TelecomTV
